slot.brief: Find the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a plane/line and then the perpendicular distance.

stem: Find the foot of the perpendicular from $P=(1,2,0)$ to the plane $2x-y+2z=3$ and the perpendicular distance.

verdicts.working: The plane normal is n=(2,-1,2), with |n|²=9. Since n·P−3=−3, the foot is H=P−[(n·P−3)/|n|²]n=(5/3,5/3,2/3), and the distance is |−3|/3=1.

working:
$F(P)=2(1)-2+0-3=-3$, $\|\vec n\|^2=9$; $H=P-\dfrac{F(P)}{9}(2,-1,2)=(\dfrac53,\dfrac53,\dfrac23)$; $PH=\dfrac{|F(P)|}{\|\vec n\|}=1$.
